- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) — adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment shows strong divergence from price trend (e.g., sentiment up but price flat or down), model tends to lag — forecast 1–2 days ahead of actual trend.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 3+ days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is consistently high but price is rising, model overfits to sentiment — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5 days to avoid overcorrection.
